subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan: ACME Retail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan: ACME Retail

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps for the PoC: 

Pain points you shared
- Search relevance is inconsistent across categories; current reranker adds latency and cost.
- High per-query latency during peak traffic (~600ms P95 today).
- Concerned about inference cost as usage scales; would like predictable unit economics.
- Data residency + SOC2 evidence needed before any production rollout.

Current stack
- Hosted on AWS (us-west-2), microservices architecture, primary app in Node/Typescript.
- Using ElasticSearch for retrieval + a lightweight reranker service.
- Existing embedding pipeline in Python (PyTorch) for nightly indexing.

Success criteria for the PoC (what ACME will evaluate)
1) Latency: P95 end-to-end rerank latency < 200ms for 5-item rerank at target QPS.
2) Cost: total inference cost for typical traffic lowered by >=30% (or demonstrably improved unit cost).
3) Quality: Precision@5 equal or improved vs current reranker on ACME internal eval set.
4) Security: SOC2 evidence + clearly documented data retention controls.

Proposed PoC scope & timeline
- Week 0 (kick-off): access, keys, and brief architecture session (1 hour).
- Week 1: Sandbox integration using Redwood SDK (Python + Node) with a small test dataset.
- Week 2: Run parallel reranking against live-ish traffic sample; collect latency/cost metrics.
- Week 3: Evaluation on ACME eval set; tune batching/quantization profile.
- Week 4: Final results, handoff plan and next steps for Dedicated/Private if successful.

Suggested owners
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (me) — commercial / schedule / contract.
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Marissa Cole — integration, sample app, runbook.
- ACME eng lead: Alex Johnson — data access and evaluation.

Integration notes (high level)
- SDKs: We support Python and Node SDKs; both provide streaming + sync endpoints.
- API compatibility: REST + WebSocket streaming; request/response formats map to standard LLM chat/generation endpoints.
- Auth: API keys for PoC; optional mTLS for Dedicated later.

I've attached a short PoC plan and a security summary for your review. Please confirm if timeline looks good and I’ll send a calendar invite for the kick-off.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0141

Attachments: PoC-Plan-ACME.xlsx, redwood-security-summary.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan: ACME Retail

Ben —

Appreciate the thorough recap — this matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications: 
- SOC2 / security docs: Can you send the most recent report and a short summary of data retention controls? We need to share with our InfoSec.
- Data residency: For the PoC, staying in us-west-2 is fine, but for production we may need EU support depending on the timeline of the pilot markets.
- Timeline: Week of Apr 5 for kick-off would work for us. Our eng lead on this will be Priya Natarajan (copied here as priya@acme-retail.com) — she’ll help with granting access and sampling traffic.

Two asks for the PoC plan: please include the exact SDK versions you recommend and a short checklist of required endpoints/credentials. Also confirm whether streaming is enabled in the Node SDK (we use streaming for intermediate tokens in UI).

If you can send the SOC2 summary and a calendar invite for Apr 6 (PST) we’ll lock in resources.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Search & Personalization, ACME Retail
alex.johnson@acme-retail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 01:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan: ACME Retail

Alex —

Great — thanks for the quick reply and the Priya intro. I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and updated the PoC workbook with recommended SDK versions and a credentials checklist. Quick answers inline: 
- SOC2: attached summary (full report available on NDA).
- SDKs: Node SDK v2.1.0 (supports streaming via WebSocket) and Python SDK v1.8.3 (sync and async support).
- Endpoints: we’ll provide a sandbox REST endpoint and a streaming WebSocket endpoint for the PoC; auth via API key.
- Data retention: For the PoC we can set retention to 7 days in the sandbox; production retention is configurable and we’ll document the defaults.

Confirmed kick-off: I’ll send an invite for Apr 6 at 10:00 AM PST. Proposed PoC milestones (short version):
- Apr 6: Kick-off + access provisioning (owners: Ben / Priya / Marissa).
- Apr 8–12: SDK integration + sample app (owner: Marissa).
- Apr 13–19: Parallel run + metrics collection (owner: Marissa / Priya).
- Apr 20: Final review and recommendation (owner: Ben / Alex).

Next steps for us: I’ll send the calendar invite and share the PoC workbook link to the Drive folder. If Priya can provision a sample traffic dump and a smaller evaluation corpus that’ll speed evaluation.

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-security-summary.pdf, PoC-Plan-ACME.xlsx, SOW_ACME_v1.pdf
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-PoC-Plan-ACME

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed PoC plan: ACME Retail

Thanks Ben — I’ll own the integration work for the PoC. Quick notes / plan on my side: 
- Languages: I’ll deliver a sample app in Node (Typescript) and Python (async) that demonstrates retrieval + rerank using the Node SDK v2.1.0 and Python v1.8.3.
- Streaming: confirm Node SDK supports token-streaming hooks; I’ll include a minimal UI example.
- Metrics: I’ll add latency instrumentation (p50/p95), batch size profiling, and a cost-estimation worksheet in the PoC workbook.
- Deliverables by Apr 12: working sample app, integration runbook, and collected metrics.

I’ll post PRs to the PoC Drive folder and ping Priya for the sample traffic.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
